title: Etiquette on the stand and behind the shooter
summary: Turns, quiet, readiness and no coaching: how to behave when you shoot and when someone else does.

body.html: In a competition, the members of a squad take the stand in turn. Do not step up until the previous shooter has left and it is your turn. When you are called, be ready at once: gun, enough cartridges for the whole round, glasses and ear protection.
When ready, the shooter gives a call, for example “Pull!” or “Ready!”. Do not keep the squad waiting: each discipline has a time limit. Details are in The call, time limits and lateness.

html.sporting: You have at most 15 seconds between singles or between doubles. Going over it brings a warning first, then penalties.
html.compak: You have at most 10 seconds to call, counted from the shot at the previous station's target. The first time is noted as a warning; a repeat in the same round is penalised.

body.html: A shooter on the stand needs full concentration, from loading until the gun is opened after the last shot. The rules let the waiting shooters stand close to the stand, but they must not disturb the one who is shooting. In practice that means: talk quietly or not at all, no sudden movements where the shooter can see you, guns open, phones silent and in a pocket. The rules say nothing about phones, but many shooting grounds expect this courtesy.
Small noises matter too. Do not snap a gun shut or take a phone call behind someone who is shooting.

Everyone who is not shooting stays behind the stand, never beside it or in front of it: spectators, coaches, interpreters, and in Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ the rest of the squad. In Compak® Sporting each station (numbered shooting place) has a Firing Angle Limiter (F.A.L.): a frame around the shooter that stops the barrels swinging too far. On many grounds the Sporting™ stands have a cage, a frame that does the same job. People who are not shooting wait behind the cage or F.A.L., where the barrels cannot point. In Compak® Sporting the squad stands side by side, each shooter on their own station inside its F.A.L. The shooter who is waiting stands behind station 1, and a shooter who has finished waits without disturbing the next one.

If you disturb a shooter, the rules step in. When the referee sees that a shooter was clearly disturbed, the target is declared a No Bird (it does not count) and is thrown again. Do not mount the gun and swing it as if at a target (mock shooting) while a squad member is shooting. In Sporting™ this is not allowed anywhere at the ground. Only the shooter whose turn it is shoots, and only at his or her own target.
Animals sometimes cross the shooting area. Do not aim or shoot at them: both rulebooks forbid it, and in Sporting™ deliberately shooting at a live animal can lead to expulsion.
During a competition nobody may tell a shooter how to shoot. The rules call this coaching. The shooter gets a yellow card, and the referee sends the person giving advice out of the shooting area.

After shooting, open the gun and take out the empty cases; put them in the bin if there is one. If you shoot a semi-automatic, pick up your ejected cases when you leave the stand. Thanking the referee and the squad is a good habit.

notes.html: For you this lesson is practical. Stop talking when your guest steps onto the stand, even in the middle of a sentence. Do not answer questions while the gun is closed. Speak again only when the gun is open: between targets, between pairs, or after the stand. A missed piece of advice costs less than a pair spoiled by your voice.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.meaning: The shooter is on the stand; everyone stops talking.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Wait until he’s opened his gun.
phrases.meaning: Nobody talks or moves until the shooter has finished and opened the gun.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Stand right behind me so you can see what I see.
phrases.meaning: In training the coach wants you directly behind, out of the swing.

phrases.speaker: referee
phrases.en: Keep out of his line, please.
phrases.meaning: You are in the shooter’s view or near the barrels’ path; move back.

key_points.html: Take the stand only in your turn and be ready at once
Quiet, still, guns open, phones silent behind the shooter
Not shooting? Stay behind the stand, cage or F.A.L., never beside or in front
Shoot only at your own target, not at animals
Coaching during a competition is forbidden

did_you_know.html: In Sporting™ the rules name the calls “ready” and “pull”. Whatever word you use, many coaches suggest keeping the call clear and the same each time.

quiz.q: When may you step onto the stand?

options.text: As soon as the previous shooter has fired his last shot
When the stand is free and it is your turn
Together with the shooter before you, to save time

quiz.explain: You step up only once the previous shooter has left the stand and it is your turn.

quiz.q: May a friend give a shooter advice during a competition?

options.text: Yes, if he whispers it between targets
Only if the friend is a qualified coach
No: it counts as coaching and is penalised

quiz.explain: Coaching during a competition is forbidden for everyone, coaches included: the shooter gets a yellow card.

quiz.q: A loud phone call behind the stand clearly disturbs the shooter at the moment of the shot. What may the referee decide?

options.text: No Bird: the target is thrown again
Nothing, phones are not in the rules

quiz.explain: If the referee sees the shooter was clearly disturbed, the target is a No Bird.
